security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG applies misaligned atomicity granule PMA atomicity guarantees only to 32-bit instruction encodings (base ISAs, F/D/Q loads/stores/AMOs) but fails to apply the same single-memory-operation atomicity guarantee to their compressed (RVC) counterparts (e.g., C.LW, C.SW, C.LD, C.SD, C.FLW, C.FSW, C.FLD, C.FSD). A compressed load/store within a misaligned atomicity granule region could be decomposed into multiple byte-level memory operations.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: check for misaligned access decomposition or atomicity granule logic that branches on instruction encoding width (e.g., checking only 32-bit opcodes) without also covering compressed (16-bit) encodings; look for RVC decode paths that bypass PMA atomicity checks; search for helper functions that split misaligned accesses without first checking the misaligned atomicity granule PMA
security_spec.summary: QEMU TCG may fail to honor misaligned atomicity granule PMA for RVC compressed load/store encodings, causing non-atomic multi-operation access in SMP guests where the spec mandates single atomic operation

findings.finding: gen_load() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 based on ext_zama16b (line 413-414). All 32-bit integer load instructions (LB, LH, LW, LD, LBU, LHU, LWU, LDU) call gen_load(), and the RVC compressed counterparts (C.LW, C.LD, C.LWSP, C.LDSP) are decoded to the same 32-bit opcode names in insn16.decode, so they use the identical code path. No RVC-specific bypass exists.

gen_store() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 based on ext_zama16b (line 524-525). All 32-bit integer store instructions (SB, SH, SW, SD) call gen_store(), and the RVC compressed counterparts (C.SW, C.SD, C.SWSP, C.SDSP) are decoded identically in insn16.decode, using the same code path with no RVC-specific bypass.

trans_flw() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 at line 52-53 for 32-bit FP loads. trans_c_flw() (line 85-89) delegates directly to trans_flw(), so compressed C.FLW gets the same atomicity treatment as the 32-bit FLW. No bypass.
trans_fsw() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 at line 75-76 for 32-bit FP stores. trans_c_fsw() (line 91-95) delegates directly to trans_fsw(), so compressed C.FSW gets the same atomicity treatment.

trans_fld() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 at line 58-59 (when XLEN>=64). trans_c_fld() (line 96-100) delegates directly to trans_fld(), so compressed C.FLD gets the same atomicity treatment as the 32-bit FLD. No separate RVC path.
trans_fsd() applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 at line 83-84 (when XLEN>=64). trans_c_fsd() (line 102-106) delegates directly to trans_fsd(), so compressed C.FSD gets the same atomicity treatment.
Zcb compressed load instructions (C.LBU, C.LHU, C.LH) all call gen_load() directly, which applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 when ext_zama16b is set. Same code path as 32-bit counterparts.
Zcb compressed store instructions (C.SB, C.SH) all call gen_store() directly, which applies MO_ATOM_WITHIN16 when ext_zama16b is set. Same code path as 32-bit counterparts.

The insn16.decode file maps RVC compressed load/store opcodes directly to the same trans_* functions as their 32-bit counterparts: lw→trans_lw, sw→trans_sw, ld→trans_ld, sd→trans_sd, c_fld→trans_fld, c_fsd→trans_fsd, c_flw→trans_flw, c_fsw→trans_fsw. There is no separate RVC-specific decode or translation path. Both encodings share identical atomicity treatment.

Zilsd/Zclsd 64-bit load/store on RV32 uses MO_SQ without MO_ATOM_WITHIN16. This is correct because zama16b only applies to operations of ≤MXLEN bits, and on RV32 where MXLEN=32, a 64-bit operation is excluded. The spec comment in trans_rvd.c.inc:50-55 confirms: 'zama16b applies to loads and stores of no more than MXLEN bits.'
